title: Reordered exclusion sums: conditional κ = 4.11862541e-5
body:
Reordering the leave-one-out sum construction produces more admissible retained carriers and reduces the physical wire count by **847,550**, from 178,378,409 to **177,530,859**. Under the inherited OpenAI base theorem and analytic/fixed-tape interfaces, this gives

**κ = 411862541/10000000000000 = 4.11862541e-5 > 2^-15**,
with bit saving **82375901/2000000000000**.

This is **7.0971766% above #36**, **0.4388585% above our previous #46**, and **0.3293163% above Rohan Arun's contemporaneous #47**. The rounded dyadic guarantee remains 2^-15; these are asymptotic exponent comparisons, not measured speedups.

## Construction

Sort the inputs to each prefix/suffix leave-one-out computation by increasing source-support size, breaking ties by increasing support bitmask at h=23 and decreasing support bitmask at h=25. Restore the original output indices after the computation. At h=23, ordinary totals also fold in reverse input order; h=25 retains its existing descending support order.

The local identity is unchanged: at sorted position i, prefix plus suffix sums every original input except the one at permutation position i. Restoring the original index is therefore essential. Every addition remains disjoint, and every globally shared output is checked exactly.

| Dimension | #46 retained carriers | New retained carriers | New roles |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 23 | 5,749 | 6,002 | 36,432 |
| 25 | 7,565 | 7,715 | 48,329 |

The scalar addition counts stay 37,098 and 49,119. Every paid endpoint, copied-center transformation, data block, complex-layer cost and downstream interface remains charged. The full new rank mass is 102,078,397,025, with unchanged deficit 1,846,900.

A bounded search evaluated 80 graph configurations and two matching objectives per graph. Exact rational candidate scores are retained in `search-record.json`. The weighted matching discovery uses Rohan Arun's #44 method with numerical search only; new finite carrier-use lists are pinned and independently replayed. No global optimality or exact matching-optimality claim is made.

## Proof and verification

- `make verify` passes, including the complete changed-producer replay, every dirty basis vector in both orientations, all 4,073,300 data pairs with exact rational recovery of the ten primary-prime failures, the exact projector audit, integrated tests and 18 historical patch checks.
- Exact lower moments exclude the complete #46 and #47 profiles at the new bit saving; the new upper moment is below one by more than 3.9870e-14.
- All 47 strict assembly inequalities and seven margins pass. The minimum margin exceeds κ by more than 2.2480e-14.
- Adversarial checks reject duplicated carriers, malformed matching files and invalid donors. A separate support oracle detects the incorrect sorted-index output convention.

See `research/copied-fixed/PROOF.md`, `certificate.json`, `SOURCE.json`, and `validation.json` for the local identity, complete cost accounting, source pins and verification receipt. The bit-network recurrence remains the binding component; the complex saving 717/10^7 has headroom.

## Attribution and scope

Prepared with OpenAI Codex assistance. Reuse is credited to icekylinx (#18/#32/#36), RaD / hipotures (#41), Rohan Arun (#39/#40/#42/#44, with his disclosed Anthropic Claude assistance), James Chang (#34), Dominik Scholz (#35), Zhihao Chen, Aurel Prosz / Paureel, Swapnil Jain and all retained authors and interfaces. #46 supplies the existing exact data recovery and independent replay machinery. #47 is included as a contemporaneous benchmark; this increment reuses no construction component from it.

The inherited ordered-affine compiler, fixed-tape costs, complete spectator/copy parking, balanced positional transfer and analytic/recovery interfaces still require expert review. Finite replay is not formal verification of those general interfaces or external acceptance of the full multiplication theorem. No Lean extension is claimed.

The branch includes the unmerged #46 ancestry; the incremental change can be reviewed against `71b6c960c89295e952522dd44111df9cfc51ae90`.
